Hi Priyanka — really helpful context, thank you.

Short answer: yes, we can support a temporary commit realignment and propose a graduated discount schedule tied to sustained volume. I'll summarize two pragmatic options below and then propose next steps.

Option A — Temporary front-loaded commit (preferred for fast spikes)
- Commit: 1.2B/month for Mar–Apr 2027, then auto-step to 900M/month May–Dec 2027 (aligns closely with expected baseline)
- Per-token pricing: base renewal price with a blended 8% discount applied to the additional 450M tokens during Mar–Apr only
- Retention incentive: one-time credit equal to 2 weeks of average monthly invoice (applied as account credit) if customer signs a 12-month renewal by Feb 15
- Rationale: gives Clarity runway to stabilize new flows without locking a permanent higher unit price

Option B — Tiered committed uplift (preferred for predictable spend)
- Commit: 900M/month for the 12-month term with a growth band allowing up to 1.2B/month without immediate reprice
- Per-token pricing: deeper per-token discount once you cross the 1.0B/month threshold in any billing month (6% incremental discount on tokens above 1.0B, cumulative up to a 12% max)
- Retention incentive: extended trial of our Premium Observability (30 days) + 4 hours of onboarding support
- Rationale: smoother uplift curve and predictable unit economics for procurement

Notes / constraints:
- We typically limit renewal uplift > 25% on list unit price without an executive approval — that said, structured credits + tiered discounts can achieve budget smoothing without deep list price cuts.
- Any long-term commit change will be documented as an amendment to the current contract (we've attached a draft amendment to show mechanics).

If either option looks reasonable, I can loop in Finance (Neha) to confirm margin/discount runway and get a quick legal amendment drafted. Would you be available for a 30-minute call Thursday PST to align?

Best,
